videos.title: Can Britain afford to lead European defence? | FT
videos.description:
As Russia expands its campaign for hybrid warfare, what can Britain and Europe do to respond? Recorded onboard the Royal Navy aircraft carrier HMS Prince of Wales docked in Oslo, host Lucy Fisher is joined by FT UK chief political commentator Robert Shrimsley and defence correspondent Charles Clover.

Together, they assess Europe’s response to Moscow's grey-zone tactics and the strategic role of the Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) - a grouping of northern European countries led by Britain including the Nordics, Baltics and the Netherlands. Is it a focused response to the threat of Russia in the north, or could it weaken the power of Nato? 

And we hear from the secretary of state for defence, Wes Streeting, who told the FT this week that the UK and Russia need new back channels to avoid “miscalculation”. Plus, how does Britain balance its ambitious defence spending commitments against tight domestic budgets and political pressure?

This week’s episode is supported by Equinor. Everything we discuss is editorially independent.

What happens when two institutions with a shared commitment to transforming lives and communities come together to advance global development?

Historically Black Colleges and Universities have a distinguished legacy of developing global leaders, advancing scientific discovery, fostering entrepreneurship, and driving economic and social transformation in the United States and around the world. videos.title: The Truth About How Data Centers Use Water And Power To Keep Cool
videos.description:
U.S. voters passed 40 ballot measures putting limits on AI data centers this week, as huge 1GW AI data centers from OpenAI, Meta, SpaceXAI, Amazon, Google and more push up water and power bills and put a strain on local resources. One of the issues that continues to come up is water usage, which is needed to cool the GPUs inside data centers running AI workloads. Closed-loop liquid cooling keeps water use low inside many modern AI data centers, but external cooling is still needed to move heat outside of the buildings and that requires large amounts of power or water in hot climates. CNBC visited data centers and spoke to researchers to find out the truth about how data centers use water.

videos.title: The 'Socialist' Bank Thriving In Trump Country
videos.description:
Progressive political candidates have clamored to launch public banks in the lead-up to the 2026 midterm elections. However, there is just one active example in the United States: the Bank of North Dakota. Chartered in 1919, this bank uses tax revenue from the state to fund and execute strategic economic development priorities for North Dakota. The bank has assisted in sales of fossil fuel assets, a presidential library, and general lending to citizens and businesses in need. CNBC's Garrett Downs reports on this “socialist experiment” unfolding deep in Trump country.

videos.title: From Local Prices to the Global Economy: The International Comparison Program
videos.description:
How do we compare economies beyond exchange rates? Purchasing power parities (PPPs) provide a clearer picture of global development, poverty, and inequality. The International Comparison Program, or ICP, is one of the world’s largest statistical collaborations—bringing together a multitude of agencies and experts to measure and compare economic activity across nearly 200 economies. Learn how the ICP is shaping the future of global economic measurement—ensuring that better data leads to better policies, smarter investments, and more informed decisions worldwide.

videos.title: Why The Measles Outbreak Signals A Bigger Problem In The U.S.
videos.description:
The U.S. is on track to lose its official measles-free elimination status, as cases have soared across the country. Health experts warn that this could be indicative of more problems to come. Vaccination rates for a variety of diseases – that have been largely pushed out of the U.S. – have been falling in recent years. Steeper declines could lead to millions of new cases in the coming years, according to scientific prediction models. Watch the video to learn about what this means for public health.
